scope: Three-file generator, generator controls and generated Windows preparation step metadata-authentication delta only.

observed_failure.failure: GitHub public release-by-tag metadata request rejected by unauthenticated runner-IP API rate limit. Failure occurred at Windows Lean toolchain setup before final proof/H0/lifecycle qualification.
observed_failure.cause_boundary: The retained API response directly identifies rate limiting; this review does not claim successful authenticated retry or final Windows artifact qualification.

confirmed_properties: The workflow keeps contents: read and adds only the built-in github.token as GH_TOKEN in the single Windows Lean setup step. No PAT, new external secret, job/workflow-wide token environment, write permission or publication path is introduced.
A missing or blank GH_TOKEN fails before the metadata request; there is no unauthenticated fallback or weakened qualification path.

Authorization Bearer, GitHub JSON Accept and API version headers are local to the exact HTTPS api.github.com leanprover/elan release-by-tag request. MaximumRedirection 0 blocks forwarding to another endpoint.
No persistent web session, default request headers or PreserveAuthorizationOnRedirect switch is introduced. The only -Headers call is metadata retrieval.

Finally clears the header hashtable, removes its variable and removes both GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN from the step process environment before asset download, archive extraction, installer execution or elan children. The credential itself retains GitHub per-job lifetime; cleanup narrows local exposure rather than changing token expiry.
The public browser_download_url archive request remains unauthenticated and receives neither headers nor session; no token is passed in command-line arguments, GITHUB_ENV, outputs or explicit logs.
Elan tag v4.2.2, exactly-one Windows asset selection, SHA256 metadata shape check, downloaded-byte hash comparison and pinned formal/asert/lean-toolchain install/execution checks remain unchanged.
The generator uses exact original anchors inside the Windows job only; changed tag/metadata-origin anchors require fresh review. Generated workflow remains bound by full-string generator equality.

Three new policy tests check metadata-only header routing/cleanup, reject missing token/redirect guard/credential cleanup or authenticated asset mutations, and reject changed historical metadata/tag anchors.
All inherited nine preparation jobs, proof/security/formal gates, read-only publication posture and unchanged release workflow remain intact.

primary_sources.supports: Built-in per-job installation token, repository scope and configurable least-privilege permissions.
Release-by-tag metadata endpoint; read-only public metadata lookup.
Explicit request headers and redirect limits; authorization-on-redirect behavior.
Process environment inheritance by child processes and removal through Env provider.

limitations: Source and finite local text-policy review only. Authenticated metadata retrieval and Windows PowerShell execution have not been observed for the new source.
Read-only authentication avoids the unauthenticated IP quota; it does not guarantee API availability or eliminate authenticated quotas. Requests continue to fail closed.
Archive SHA verification retains the existing API-supplied digest trust model; this change does not introduce an independently hardcoded archive digest.
No reviewer source changes, native build, proof execution, node operation, commit, push, dispatch, publication, activation or deployment performed. Fresh refreeze and exact-source CI remain required.
